experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and arches along the golden coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's dramatic geology.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Visit a local winery in the Lagoa wine region, the heart of Algarve viticulture, for a guided tasting of regional wines including Arinto and Negra Mole varieties. Pair your wines with a traditional Cataplana seafood stew prepared by a local chef.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park spanning 60km of coastline. Discover barrier islands, flamingo colonies, and secluded barrier beaches only accessible by boat, with stops for swimming and snorkeling in calm lagoon waters.

experiences.name: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the Moorish red sandstone castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, followed by a guided food walk through the historic old town. Sample local specialties including carob products, medronho brandy, almond sweets, and fresh orange juice at traditional market stalls.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Eva Bus or Rede Expressos coach from Faro Airport to Lagos (approx. €5-7, ~1.5 hours). Check in to Boutique Taghostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva. Freshen up and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snack
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snack
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a 24h petrol station kiosk near the bus terminal or a kebab shop near Lagos center (€3-5)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Faro to Lagos bus ticket online at rede-expressos.pt to save time. The last bus from Faro to Lagos departs around midnight — confirm schedule in advance. Keep arrival light and stress-free.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a slow start, walk to the historic old town of Lagos. Explore the free Ponta da Bandeira Fort exterior and stroll along the city walls. Visit the Igreja de Santo António (small entry fee ~€2) and the adjacent Municipal Museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 15 minutes south to Meia Praia or take a short taxi/Uber to Praia Dona Ana — one of the most stunning beaches in the Algarve with golden cliffs and turquoise water. Swim, relax, and soak in the scenery. Entry is free.
day_by_day.evening: Head back into Lagos old town. Wander the cobblestone streets around Praça Gil Eanes. Enjoy the lively atmosphere as locals and travelers mix in the squares.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mota or a local café near the hostel — coffee and pastel de nata for under €2
meals.lunch: Grab a prego (steak sandwich) or bifana at a local tasca near the market for €3-5
meals.dinner: O Camilo or Restaurante Adega da Marina — look for the prato do dia (dish of the day) which typically costs €7-10 including bread, drink, and dessert

day_by_day.notes: September is still warm (24-27°C) with fewer crowds than August — perfect beach weather. Bring sunscreen and a reusable water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free self-guided walk along the Ponta da Piedade coastal trail starting from Lagos town center (~2km walk). Marvel at the dramatic sea stacks, grottos, and arches. Arrive early to avoid crowds and get the best light for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a kayak or join a budget group kayak tour from Ponta da Piedade (€15-20 per person) to explore the sea caves and hidden grottos up close. Alternatively, hire a small fisherman's boat for a short grotto tour (~€10-15 per person negotiated locally).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Visit the Mercado de Lagos (covered market) if still open for fresh local produce. Relax at the hostel, meet fellow travelers, and enjoy the hostel's common area.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast if included, or a local padaria (bakery) — toast, juice, and coffee for €2-3
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the Mercado de Lagos — local cheese, bread, fruit, and olives for €4-6
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Vivant or a local grill house — grilled sardines or chicken piri-piri with salad and fries for €8-12

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade is walkable from the hostel in about 30-40 minutes or a short €5 Uber ride. Wear sturdy shoes for the cliff path. The kayak tours are weather-dependent.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus (Vamus Algarve, ~€2-3) or carpool/rideshare to Sagres, about 30km west of Lagos. Visit the impressive Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry) — a 15th-century fortress at the southwestern tip of Europe with sweeping Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Praia do Martinhal or Praia da Mareta near Sagres village — quieter, wilder beaches with dramatic scenery. Swim and relax. Explore the village of Sagres which has a laid-back surfer vibe.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Enjoy a relaxed evening in the old town. Check out the free live music that often plays in the squares on Friday evenings.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at the hostel or a café in Lagos before departure
meals.lunch: A Sagres village café or snack bar — fresh fish sandwich or soup for €4-6
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso or similar local tasca in Lagos old town — cataplana (seafood stew) or grilled fish for €9-13

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is windier and cooler than Lagos — bring a light jacket. The Vamus bus runs regularly between Lagos and Sagres. Check the return schedule to avoid being stranded.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Lagos Saturday market (Mercado de Levante) for local produce, crafts, and regional products. A great place to stock up on affordable snacks and souvenirs. Then explore Praia do Camilo — a small, secluded beach accessible via wooden stairs cut into the cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Luz, a charming beach village 6km west of Lagos (reachable by Vamus bus ~€1.50 or a 20-min bike ride). Enjoy the wide sandy beach, swim, and explore the small village with its whitewashed church.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Saturday night is lively — enjoy the buzzing atmosphere of Rua 25 de Abril (the main bar street). Have a drink at one of the outdoor terraces without overspending.

meals.breakfast: Market breakfast — fresh fruit, local cheese, and bread bought at the market for €3-4
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar at Praia da Luz — grilled fish or salad for €7-10
meals.dinner: Self-catering from the market or a supermarket (Pingo Doce or Lidl nearby) — cook a simple meal at the hostel kitchen for €4-6 per person

day_by_day.notes: Renting a bike from a Lagos rental shop (€10-15/day) is a great budget way to reach Praia da Luz and explore the coastline. Saturday evenings in Lagos can be noisy — use earplugs if you're a light sleeper.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Catch the train from Lagos to Silves (€3-4, ~40 minutes with a change at Tunes). Visit the stunning red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry) with panoramic views over the orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves old town — the Gothic Cathedral (free entry), the Roman bridge, and the charming riverside. Visit a local wine shop or the Silves Wine Festival remnants (if still running in September). The Algarve region produces excellent affordable wines — pick up a bottle for €4-6.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train. Enjoy a quiet Sunday evening — sit by the waterfront at Avenida dos Descobrimentos and watch the boats on the Bensafrim River estuary.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or café in Lagos before departure — coffee and pastry for €2
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — famous for affordable fresh seafood, prato do dia for €8-10
meals.dinner: Supermarket picnic or hostel kitchen meal — local Algarve wine, cheese, and charcuterie for €5-7

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a fantastic budget day trip — low entry fees and very authentic. The train journey is scenic and affordable. Wine tasting interest: Silves has several wine shops where you can taste local Algarve wines for free or minimal cost.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Praia Porto de Mós — a beautiful, less-crowded beach about 3km south of Lagos, reachable by a scenic cliff walk or short bus ride. Enjoy the golden cliffs, clear water, and peaceful morning atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (book in advance, ~30km east of Lagos). Take a budget wine tour and tasting (€10-15 per person) through the Algarve vineyards. This is one of the most accessible wineries for budget travelers in the region. Arrange transport via shared taxi or rideshare.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the hostel. Share wine and stories with fellow travelers in the common area.

meals.breakfast: Local café near the hostel — galão (milky coffee) and croissant for €2-3
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for the beach — supermarket supplies for €4-5
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Galeão in Lagos — traditional Portuguese cuisine, main courses €8-12

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales offers some of the best value wine experiences in the Algarve. Book ahead via their website. If transport is difficult, ask the hostel about organized wine tour day trips which sometimes run from Lagos.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha. Catch the Vamus bus from Lagos to Portimão (€2-3, ~30 minutes). Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays, €3 other days) — an excellent museum in a converted sardine canning factory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Praia da Rocha — a wide, dramatic beach with impressive rock formations. Swim and relax. Explore the clifftop promenade with views over the beach. Visit the small Fortaleza de Santa Catarina (free entry) at the eastern end of the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Portimão's waterfront and the lively Largo 1° de Dezembro square. Portimão is famous for its grilled sardines — enjoy them fresh from a riverside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagos before departure — coffee and toast for €2
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Praia da Rocha — prego or bifana sandwich for €4-5
meals.dinner: Riverside sardine restaurant in Portimão — grilled sardines with bread and salad for €7-10. Return to Lagos by bus after dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Portimão's sardine grilling tradition is iconic — the smell of sardines on charcoal grills along the waterfront is unforgettable. September is still great sardine season.

day_by_day.morning: Lazy beach morning at Meia Praia — the long sandy beach just east of Lagos, easily walkable or reachable by a short ferry across the river (€1 each way). Meia Praia stretches for 4km and is less crowded than the cliff beaches. Perfect for a long morning swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos and take a free self-guided walking tour of the historic center. Visit the Slave Market (Mercado de Escravos) — the first slave market in Europe, now a museum (€3 entry). Reflect on the city's complex history. Browse the local craft shops along Rua 25 de Abril.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost Fado music performance — check local listings for free Fado nights at bars or cultural centers in Lagos. Fado is Portugal's soulful national music genre.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen or local padaria — yogurt, fruit, and coffee for €2-3
meals.lunch: Tasca near the market — soup and bread for €2-3, main for €5-7
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco — petiscos (Portuguese tapas) style dining, share plates for €6-10 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Meia Praia ferry is a charming local experience and very cheap. Check the hostel notice board for free cultural events happening in Lagos this week.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Tavira — one of the most beautiful and authentic towns in the Algarve, about 120km east of Lagos. Take the train (€8-10 each way, ~2 hours). Explore the Roman bridge, the castle ruins (free), and the charming whitewashed old town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the local ferry from Tavira to Ilha de Tavira (€1.50 each way) — a stunning barrier island beach with crystal-clear water and a relaxed atmosphere. Swim and relax on one of the Algarve's most beautiful natural beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tavira town for a stroll and early dinner before catching the train back to Lagos. Tavira has a more authentic, less touristy feel than Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Quick coffee and pastry at Lagos train station café for €2
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Ilha de Tavira — fresh fish or salad for €7-9
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bica in Tavira — traditional Algarve cuisine, prato do dia for €8-11

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is a longer day trip but absolutely worth it for its authenticity and beauty. Check train times carefully — the last train back to Lagos is usually around 20:00-21:00. Book return tickets in advance at cp.pt.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Lagos Fish Market (Mercado de Peixe) early morning to see the daily catch being sold — a vibrant local experience. Then take a free walk along the Lagos waterfront promenade (Avenida dos Descobrimentos) and the marina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget group wine tasting session — check with the hostel or local tour operators for afternoon wine tasting events in or near Lagos. Alternatively, visit a local wine shop like Garrafeira do Mercado for a self-guided tasting of Algarve wines (bottles from €4-8). Pair with local cheese and presunto (cured ham).
day_by_day.evening: Friday night in Lagos — enjoy the lively old town atmosphere. Have pre-dinner drinks at a rooftop bar or terrace. Explore the nightlife on Rua 25 de Abril without overspending — many bars have happy hour deals.

meals.breakfast: Market fresh produce — fruit, bread, and local honey for €3-4
meals.lunch: Tasca do Celso or similar — grilled chicken or fish with rice for €7-9
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina — fresh seafood platter or cataplana for €10-14

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos fish market is best visited before 9am for the full experience. Friday evenings are lively — a great opportunity to meet other travelers and enjoy the social atmosphere of the hostel.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach day — revisit your favorite beach or try Praia do Burgau, a charming small beach in a fishing village 12km west of Lagos (reachable by Vamus bus ~€2). Enjoy a long, relaxed morning swim in the warm September sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for last-minute souvenir shopping. Budget-friendly souvenirs: local wine (€4-8), flor de sal (sea salt, €3-5), almond sweets (€3-5), and handmade ceramics. Visit the Saturday market one last time if it's running.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner with fellow hostel travelers. Organize a group dinner at a local restaurant to share costs. Toast to the trip with a glass of local Algarve wine or a Sagres beer.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café — full Portuguese breakfast for €4-6
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia do Burgau — grilled fish or salad for €7-10
meals.dinner: Group dinner at Restaurante O Galeão or similar — set menu or shared dishes for €10-15 per person including wine

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight and prepare for departure tomorrow. Keep receipts for any VAT refund claims on purchases over €50. Check bus/transfer options to Faro Airport for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos. Take a last slow walk through the old town — visit Praça Gil Eanes, grab a final pastel de nata and coffee at your favorite café. Soak in the atmosphere one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hostel (standard checkout 11:00 — ask about late checkout if needed, usually €5-10 extra). Store luggage at the hostel if your departure is later. Take the Rede Expressos or Eva Bus from Lagos to Faro Airport (€5-7, ~1.5 hours). Arrive at the airport with plenty of time.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days in the Algarve — beaches, wine, history, and authentic Portuguese culture.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão at a Lagos café — €2-3
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hostel kitchen using leftover supplies, or a café near the bus station for €5-7
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate: Accommodation at Taghostel (hostel dorm ~€20-30/night x 12 nights = €240-360), food (~€20-30/day = €260-390), transport (~€80-120 total for buses/trains), activities (~€60-80), wine/souvenirs (~€40-60). Total estimated budget: €680-1,010 for 13 days — very achievable for a budget-conscious traveler.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the airport shuttle or pre-booked taxi (~1 hour) to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos. Check in, freshen up, and grab a late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour café or the hostel's common area. Get oriented with a map of Lagos for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at Café Correia or a nearby tasca open late in Lagos centro – try a simple bifana (pork sandwich) and a local beer

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – just arrival and settling in. Confirm all upcoming bookings and set an alarm for an early start on Day 2. The hostel is centrally located in Lagos, walking distance to most town amenities.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a leisurely breakfast in Lagos, then explore the historic old town on foot. Visit the Igreja de Santo António (a stunning gilded baroque church) and the adjacent Municipal Museum. Stroll along the city walls and the Slave Market (Mercado de Escravos), one of Europe's first slave markets, now a sobering museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, a long golden beach just east of Lagos, easily reachable by a short taxi or bike ride. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and relaxing on one of the Algarve's most accessible and beautiful beaches. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella for comfort.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos town center. Wander the cobblestone streets of the Zona Histórica as the evening cools. Enjoy dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mota near the hostel – fresh pastéis de nata, coffee, and toast (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Meia Praia – grilled sardines, salad, and a cold Sagres beer (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina – traditional Portuguese grilled fish and cataplana dishes (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a Lagos Card or ask the hostel about bike rentals for easy mobility around town. September weather is typically warm and sunny – perfect beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short bus or taxi to Ponta da Piedade, Lagos's most iconic landmark. Explore the dramatic golden limestone rock formations, sea arches, and grottos along the clifftop walking path. Arrive early (before 9:30 AM) to beat the crowds and enjoy the best light for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Ponta da Piedade, take a short boat trip (€15–20) into the sea caves and grottos below the cliffs – a must-do Lagos experience. Afterward, relax at Praia do Camilo, a small sheltered beach tucked between the cliffs, accessible via a wooden staircase.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Lagos for a relaxed evening. Browse the artisan shops and galleries along Rua 25 de Abril. Enjoy a sundowner drink at a rooftop bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Atlântico in Lagos – scrambled eggs, fresh juice, and coffee (€6–8)
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia do Camilo or pack a picnic from the local Pingo Doce supermarket (€8–12)
meals.dinner: No Pátio Restaurant – cozy courtyard setting, excellent grilled octopus and local wines (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the clifftop walk at Ponta da Piedade. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water. The boat trips depart from the beach below the lighthouse – negotiate directly with local boatmen for the best price.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim experience. Travel east along the coast (approx. 1.5 hours by bus or rental car via Lagoa) to Praia da Marinha, consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. The guided coastal hike explores dramatic limestone cliffs, hidden sea caves, and natural arches along the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, descend to Praia da Marinha beach itself for a well-earned swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters. Explore the small sea caves accessible at low tide. Spend a couple of hours relaxing on the beach before heading back toward Lagos.
day_by_day.evening: Stop in the town of Lagoa on the way back for a pre-dinner stroll and a glass of local wine at a wine bar. Return to Lagos for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel or a nearby café before departure – toast, fruit, and coffee (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia da Marinha – fresh seafood sandwich and cold drink (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Camilo in Lagos – fresh catch of the day with local vegetables and house wine (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike is a featured experience – book in advance. Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring plenty of water. Check tide times before descending to the beach caves. A rental car makes this day much easier and opens up flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a bus to Carvoeiro, a charming fishing village with a picturesque beach. Explore the Algar Seco rock formations – a stunning natural sculpture garden of eroded limestone cliffs with walkways, arches, and sea pools. Walk the short coastal boardwalk and enjoy the dramatic scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on the Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour – one of the Algarve's most iconic experiences. Paddle from Praia de Benagil through the turquoise waters and into the legendary Benagil Cave, a cathedral-like sea cave with a natural skylight opening in its domed ceiling. The tour typically lasts 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Shower and change, then head out for a lively Saturday evening in Lagos's old town. The town has a vibrant nightlife scene – enjoy tapas and drinks at a bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Padaria Moderna in Lagos – fresh bread, cheese, ham, and coffee (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Light snack before the kayak tour – energy bar and fruit, or a quick bite at Praia de Benagil's beach café (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco – excellent petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and regional wines in a cozy setting (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour is a featured experience – book well in advance as it sells out quickly, especially on weekends. Bring a waterproof bag for your phone and camera. The cave is only accessible by sea, so this kayak tour is the best way to experience it fully.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slow Sunday morning in Lagos. Sleep in, have a leisurely breakfast, and visit the weekly Mercado Municipal (covered market) for fresh local produce, cheeses, smoked meats, and pastries. Pick up some local snacks and a bottle of Algarve wine to take back to the hostel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Luz, a relaxed beach village about 6 km west of Lagos (reachable by bus or taxi). Spend the afternoon on the wide sandy beach, swimming and sunbathing. The village has a lovely promenade and a laid-back atmosphere – perfect for a restful Sunday.
day_by_day.evening: Dine in Praia da Luz before returning to Lagos, or head back to Lagos for dinner. Sunday evenings in Lagos are quieter and pleasant for a relaxed meal.

meals.breakfast: Mercado Municipal Lagos – fresh fruit, local cheese, and a coffee from a market stall (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Praia da Luz beach – grilled chicken piri-piri and salad (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Mullens Restaurant in Lagos – popular mid-range spot with excellent steaks and seafood, good wine list (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a good day to recharge. The market is busiest in the morning, so arrive by 9–10 AM for the best selection. Praia da Luz is a great alternative to busier Lagos beaches and has excellent snorkeling near the black rock formations at the eastern end.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Sagres, the southwestern tip of continental Europe, about 30 km from Lagos (bus or rental car). Visit the imposing Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress perched dramatically on the cliffs where Henry the Navigator planned Portugal's Age of Discovery. Explore the windswept promontory and the giant wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos).
day_by_day.afternoon: From Sagres, drive or walk to Cabo de São Vicente – the most southwestern point of continental Europe. Stand at the edge of the continent with dramatic Atlantic views. Then visit Praia do Beliche, a wild and beautiful beach sheltered by cliffs near the cape, for a swim in the Atlantic.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a quiet evening with dinner at a local restaurant. Consider picking up a bottle of Algarve wine from a shop to enjoy on the hostel terrace.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagos before departure – croissant, juice, and coffee (€5–7)
meals.lunch: A Sagres – restaurant in Sagres village with fresh seafood and stunning views (€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bica in Lagos – traditional Portuguese home cooking, excellent value (€15–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente can be windy even in September – bring a light jacket. The area is also famous for surfing; Praia do Tonel near Sagres is a popular surf beach if you want to watch or try a lesson. The last bus back to Lagos from Sagres is in the early evening – check the schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience – a featured highlight of the trip. Travel to the Lagoa wine region (approx. 45 minutes from Lagos), the heart of Algarve viticulture. Enjoy a guided winery tour learning about the unique terroir, grape varieties (Negra Mole, Crato Branco), and winemaking traditions of the region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine experience with a tasting of several Algarve wines paired with a traditional Cataplana lunch – a slow-cooked seafood and pork stew prepared in a copper clam-shaped pot, one of the Algarve's most iconic dishes. Take time to purchase a few bottles to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos in the late afternoon, pleasantly relaxed from the wine tasting. Enjoy a light evening stroll along the marina and waterfront. Have a casual dinner and an early night.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or nearby café – yogurt, fruit, and coffee (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Included in the Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience – traditional cataplana with wine pairings
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso in Lagos – light tapas and local cheese board to complement the day's wine theme (€14–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience is a featured experience – book in advance. This is a full sensory experience combining wine education, local gastronomy, and cultural immersion. Designate a driver if renting a car, or arrange transport through the experience provider or hostel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Silves for the Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk experience. Travel inland about 45 minutes from Lagos to Silves, the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Begin with a guided tour of the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves, one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal, with panoramic views over the orange groves and hills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the guided food walk through Silves's charming old town. Sample local specialties including medronho (arbutus berry brandy), local cheeses, smoked sausages, almond sweets, and traditional pastries at artisan shops and local producers. Visit the Gothic Cathedral of Silves and the Archaeological Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed evening – perhaps a sunset walk along the Lagos waterfront or a drink at a rooftop bar. Have dinner at a restaurant you haven't tried yet.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Lagos before departure – toast with local honey and coffee (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Included in the Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk – tastings and samples throughout the tour
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião in Lagos – upscale mid-range dining with excellent regional cuisine and wine list (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk is a featured experience – book in advance. Silves is also famous for its annual Medieval Fair (usually August), but September is a great time to visit without the crowds. The town has a lovely riverside area along the Arade River worth exploring after the tour.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Tavira, often called the most beautiful town in the Algarve, about 1.5 hours east of Lagos by train (change at Faro). Explore the elegant town with its Roman bridge, whitewashed churches, and Moorish-influenced architecture. Visit the Castelo de Tavira for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Tavira, take a short ferry or water taxi to Ilha de Tavira, a stunning barrier island beach within the Ria Formosa Natural Park. Spend the afternoon on this pristine, unspoiled beach – one of the finest in the Algarve. The calm, shallow waters are perfect for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tavira for a sunset drink along the Gilão River before catching the train back to Lagos. Arrive back in Lagos for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Central in Tavira upon arrival – fresh pastries and coffee (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Beach restaurant on Ilha de Tavira – fresh grilled fish, salad, and local wine (€18–24 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Galeão in Lagos – reliable mid-range seafood and meat dishes (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The train from Lagos to Tavira requires a change at Faro – total journey about 1.5–2 hours each way. Check the CP (Comboios de Portugal) schedule in advance. The ferry to Ilha de Tavira runs frequently in summer and early autumn. Bring cash as some island facilities don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the western Algarve coast with a visit to Praia do Amado, one of the best surf beaches in Portugal, about 40 km north of Sagres. Even if you don't surf, it's a spectacular wild beach with powerful Atlantic waves and dramatic scenery. Consider a beginner surf lesson (€35–45) at one of the surf schools on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to the Costa Vicentina, part of the Southwest Alentejo and Vicentine Coast Natural Park – one of Europe's last unspoiled coastlines. Visit Praia de Odeceixe, a unique beach where a river meets the sea, creating a natural lagoon perfect for swimming. The surrounding cliffs and dunes are breathtaking.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for the evening. Enjoy a final Friday night out in Lagos's vibrant old town – the town comes alive on weekends with street musicians, outdoor bars, and a festive atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagos before departure – full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, ham, and coffee (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia do Amado – burger, salad, and cold drink (€12–15)
meals.dinner: A Forja Restaurant in Lagos – beloved local institution with excellent grilled meats and fish (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: A rental car is strongly recommended for this day to access the more remote western beaches. The Costa Vicentina is protected from development, making it feel wild and authentic. September is ideal – warm but less crowded than peak summer. Praia de Odeceixe is about 1 hour north of Lagos.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final relaxed morning in Lagos. Revisit your favorite spots, do some last-minute souvenir shopping along Rua 25 de Abril and Rua Cândido dos Reis. Pick up local products: Algarve wine, medronho, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos), and dried figs. Visit the Lagos Marina for a morning coffee with waterfront views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take one last swim at Praia dos Estudantes or Praia do Pinhão, two small beaches just a short walk from the Lagos town center. These intimate beaches tucked between golden cliffs are perfect for a final Algarve beach experience. Alternatively, rent a kayak or SUP board for a couple of hours.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the final evening with a special dinner at one of Lagos's best restaurants. Splurge slightly on a memorable meal with excellent Algarve wine. After dinner, enjoy a farewell drink at a rooftop bar watching the stars over the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mota – a return to your Day 2 breakfast spot for nostalgia – pastéis de nata and coffee (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Mercado de Lagos food hall – browse various stalls for a final taste of local flavors (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vasco da Gama – upscale mid-range with exceptional seafood and regional wine pairings, perfect for a farewell dinner (€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight and prepare for departure tomorrow. Keep receipts for any VAT refund claims on purchases over €50. The hostel may offer luggage storage if you have an early checkout but late departure. Confirm your airport transfer or taxi for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast in Lagos. Take a slow morning walk through the old town one last time – the quiet Sunday morning streets have a special charm. Visit the waterfront and say goodbye to the Atlantic. Check out of the Boutique Taghostel (standard checkout is usually 11 AM – arrange luggage storage if needed).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, either head directly to Faro Airport (allow 1–1.5 hours travel time plus 2 hours before departure) or spend a couple of final hours exploring Lagos or stopping in Faro city for a brief visit to the old town (Cidade Velha) and the famous Bone Chapel (Igreja dos Ossos) near the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days in the Algarve – beaches, wine, history, and culture. Carry home memories of golden cliffs, turquoise waters, and the warm flavors of Portuguese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Final café breakfast in Lagos – fresh orange juice, coffee, and a pastel de nata (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Airport café or a quick bite in Faro old town if time allows (€10–15)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Faro Airport is approximately 1 hour from Lagos by taxi (€50–65) or shuttle bus. Book your transfer in advance, especially on a Sunday when public transport is reduced. The Algarve Express bus also connects Lagos to Faro but takes longer. Allow extra time for Sunday traffic and airport security.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and arches along the golden coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's dramatic geology.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Visit a local winery in the Lagoa wine region, the heart of Algarve viticulture, for a guided tasting of regional wines including Arinto and Negra Mole varieties. Pair your wines with a traditional Cataplana seafood stew prepared by a local chef.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park spanning 60km of coastline. Discover barrier islands, flamingo colonies, and secluded barrier beaches only accessible by boat, with stops for swimming and snorkeling in calm lagoon waters.

experiences.name: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the Moorish red sandstone castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, followed by a guided food walk through the historic old town. Sample local specialties including carob products, medronho brandy, almond sweets, and fresh orange juice at traditional market stalls.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer pre-arranged to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (approx. 1 hour drive). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome glass of local Algarve wine at the hotel's lounge bar before retiring for the night.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Light late-night charcuterie and cheese board with a glass of Algarve white wine at the hotel lounge upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm late check-in with Boutique Taghostel. Pack light for easy access to essentials upon arrival. Rest is the priority tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the hotel to recover from travel. Afterwards, take a gentle orientation stroll through Lagos old town — explore the historic Ponta da Bandeira Fort, the charming cobblestone streets, and the vibrant local market. Soak in the atmosphere of this beautiful coastal town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, Lagos's longest and most elegant beach (just 10 minutes from the hotel). Rent a premium sun lounger and parasol setup, swim in the warm Atlantic waters, and enjoy the golden September sunshine. Optionally arrange a private paddleboard or kayak rental directly on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar overlooking the Atlantic. Dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina, one of Lagos's finest seafood restaurants, known for its fresh catch, grilled octopus, and exceptional local wine list.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — fresh pastries, local cheeses, cured meats, fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch at a premium beach club on Meia Praia — grilled fish, salads, and chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina — grilled sea bass, cataplana de marisco, and a bottle of Algarve Lagoa DOC white wine

day_by_day.notes: September weather in the Algarve is typically warm and sunny (24–28°C). This is a gentle recovery day after travel. Book dinner reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim — depart from Lagos by private car (approx. 30 minutes east). Explore one of the Algarve's most breathtaking beaches, famous for its dramatic limestone cliffs, golden arches, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the scenic clifftop trail with panoramic ocean views before descending to swim in the sheltered coves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Praia da Marinha coastline, discovering hidden sea caves and rock formations accessible at low tide. Enjoy a private picnic lunch arranged by the hotel on the beach — premium charcuterie, local cheeses, fresh bread, and chilled rosé. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing in this stunning natural setting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by private transfer. Freshen up at the hotel, then enjoy dinner at No Pátio, a sophisticated Lagos restaurant celebrated for its creative Portuguese cuisine and curated wine list in a beautiful courtyard setting.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Premium hotel-arranged picnic on Praia da Marinha — artisan bread, local cheeses, Iberian ham, olives, fruit, and chilled Algarve rosé
meals.dinner: No Pátio Lagos — tasting menu with wine pairing featuring local Algarve and Alentejo wines

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring reef shoes for rocky cove swimming. Apply high-SPF sunscreen. The coastal hike is moderate difficulty — approximately 3km round trip. Book private transfer in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour — depart early from Lagos by private car to Benagil Beach (approx. 35 minutes). Join a premium small-group or private kayak tour to paddle through the world-famous Benagil Cave, one of the most spectacular sea caves on earth. Explore the cathedral-like interior with its natural skylight and golden sandy floor, accessible only by water.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Benagil Beach or nearby Praia de Carvalho, a secluded gem accessible through a cliff tunnel. Swim in the warm Atlantic waters and soak up the afternoon sun. Private transfer back to Lagos mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks on the rooftop or terrace of the hotel. Dinner at Casinha do Petisco, a beloved Lagos fine dining spot known for its innovative take on traditional Algarvian cuisine and impressive local wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure — pastries, fruit, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a local restaurant near Benagil Beach — grilled sardines, fresh salad, and local white wine
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco — chef's tasting menu with Algarve wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil kayak tour well in advance as it is extremely popular. Opt for a private tour for a premium experience. Bring waterproof bags for valuables. The cave is best visited in the morning when light streams through the natural skylight.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience — private car to the Lagoa wine region (approx. 40 minutes from Lagos). Visit a prestigious local winery for an exclusive guided tour of the vineyards and cellars, learning about the unique Algarve terroir and indigenous grape varieties such as Negra Mole and Crato Branco. Enjoy a premium guided tasting of the estate's finest wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine experience with a traditional Cataplana cooking demonstration and lunch at the winery — the iconic copper-pot seafood stew paired with the estate's wines. Explore the surrounding Lagoa countryside before private transfer back to Lagos.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Lagos. Stroll along the marina and waterfront promenade. Dinner at Restaurante Bon Vivant, a sophisticated Lagos institution known for its exceptional seafood, premium steaks, and extensive wine list.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Winery cataplana lunch — traditional Algarvian seafood cataplana with estate wine pairing
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Vivant — grilled black pork secreto, fresh lobster, and a bottle of premium Alentejo red

day_by_day.notes: This is a highlight day for wine enthusiasts. Request a private winery tour for the most exclusive experience. Purchase bottles of your favorite wines to take home — the hotel can arrange secure storage.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern tip of Europe. Private car departs Lagos (approx. 30 minutes). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres, the historic fortress where Henry the Navigator planned Portugal's Age of Discovery. Walk the windswept clifftops with breathtaking Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Cabo de São Vicente, Europe's most southwesterly point, with its iconic lighthouse and dramatic 75-meter cliffs. Watch the waves crash against the ancient rocks. Visit the local artisan market at Sagres for handcrafted souvenirs. Return to Lagos by private car.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a Lagos clifftop bar. Dinner at A Forja, a charming and highly regarded Lagos restaurant known for its traditional Portuguese recipes, fresh seafood, and warm hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant in Sagres — fresh grilled fish, local bread, and chilled Vinho Verde overlooking the Atlantic
meals.dinner: A Forja Lagos — traditional bacalhau à brás, grilled tiger prawns, and local Algarve wine

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The area is a surfer's paradise and the scenery is unlike anywhere else in Portugal. Sunset at Cabo de São Vicente is spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning in Lagos. Sleep in and enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Visit the Mercado Municipal de Lagos for a sensory experience of local produce, fresh fish, spices, and artisan goods. Pick up local honey, almonds, figs, and carob products as gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia Dona Ana — one of Lagos's most beautiful and iconic beaches, just a short walk or taxi from the hotel. Rent a premium sun lounger setup and spend the afternoon swimming in the crystal-clear waters framed by golden limestone cliffs. Optionally book a private boat tour from Lagos marina to explore the sea caves and grottos along the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Spa treatment at the hotel or a nearby luxury spa — a relaxing massage or body treatment to rejuvenate mid-trip. Dinner at Restaurante Laranjeira, an elegant Lagos fine dining restaurant with a romantic atmosphere and exceptional Portuguese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — full spread with local specialties
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch at Praia Dona Ana — fresh seafood platter, salads, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Restaurante Laranjeira — duck rice, grilled sea bream, and a curated Portuguese wine flight

day_by_day.notes: This is a planned rest and recovery day. Praia Dona Ana is within easy walking distance of the hotel. Book the spa treatment in advance. The private boat tour from Lagos marina is highly recommended for a unique perspective of the coastline.

day_by_day.morning: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk — private car to Silves (approx. 30 minutes from Lagos). Explore the magnificent Moorish red sandstone castle, one of the best-preserved in Portugal, with panoramic views over the Algarve countryside. Visit the Cathedral of Silves and the fascinating Silves Municipal Museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a guided food walk through Silves old town — taste local specialties including almond sweets, carob products, local cheeses, smoked sausages, and traditional pastries at artisan shops and local producers. Visit the Silves cork factory to learn about Portugal's world-famous cork industry.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by private car. Sunset drinks at the hotel terrace. Dinner at Vitor's Restaurant, a Lagos institution celebrated for its premium seafood, exceptional wine cellar, and impeccable service.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — one of the Algarve's most celebrated seafood restaurants, famous for its cataplana and fresh shellfish
meals.dinner: Vitor's Restaurant Lagos — lobster bisque, grilled turbot, and a premium Douro Valley red wine

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a fascinating historical town that offers a completely different perspective of the Algarve beyond the beaches. The food walk is a wonderful way to connect with local culture and gastronomy. Book Marisqueira Rui well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour — private car to Faro (approx. 1 hour from Lagos). Board a premium private boat for an exclusive cruise through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park spanning 60km of coastline. Discover hidden barrier islands, salt marshes, and diverse birdlife including flamingos, herons, and spoonbills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark on one of the pristine barrier islands — Ilha Deserta or Ilha do Farol — for swimming and relaxation on a virtually untouched beach. Enjoy a private seafood lunch on the island. Return by boat to Faro and private transfer back to Lagos.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Lagos. Visit a local wine bar for a curated tasting of Portuguese wines from different regions. Dinner at a Lagos restaurant of choice — revisit a favorite or try somewhere new.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — early start required
meals.lunch: Private seafood lunch on the barrier island — fresh oysters, clams, grilled fish, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Dom Sebastião Restaurant Lagos — traditional Algarvian cuisine with a premium wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Book a private boat tour for the most exclusive Ria Formosa experience. Bring binoculars for birdwatching. The barrier islands are some of the most pristine beaches in Portugal. September is an excellent time for this tour with warm water and fewer crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Monchique — the lush mountain village in the Serra de Monchique (approx. 45 minutes from Lagos by private car). Explore the charming village, visit the Franciscan convent ruins, and hike to Fóia, the highest peak in the Algarve (902m) with panoramic views stretching to the Atlantic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the famous Monchique thermal spa for a premium wellness experience — thermal baths, treatments, and relaxation in the healing mineral waters that have been celebrated since Roman times. Explore the local artisan shops for medronho (arbutus berry brandy), honey, and handcrafted wooden products.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by private car. Dinner at Restaurante O Camilo, perched dramatically on the cliffs above Praia do Camilo with spectacular ocean views — one of the most romantic dining settings in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Central de Monchique — traditional mountain cuisine featuring black pork, smoked meats, and local vegetables with medronho digestif
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Camilo — fresh seafood with cliffside Atlantic views and a premium Algarve wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Monchique offers a completely different landscape from the coast — lush eucalyptus and pine forests, cooler temperatures, and a peaceful mountain atmosphere. Bring a light layer for the higher altitude. Book the thermal spa in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private yacht charter from Lagos Marina — a full-day luxury sailing experience along the Algarve coastline. Depart in the morning and sail west toward Sagres or east toward Portimão, exploring sea caves, grottos, and hidden beaches accessible only by boat. Snorkeling equipment provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the yacht charter — anchor in a secluded cove for swimming, snorkeling, and sunbathing. Enjoy a premium catered lunch on board with fresh seafood, chilled wines, and artisan breads. The crew will guide you to the most spectacular spots along the coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos Marina at sunset for a magical golden-hour arrival. Freshen up at the hotel. Farewell-style premium dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina — a celebratory meal with a premium wine pairing to mark the penultimate full day.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at Boutique Taghostel before departure
meals.lunch: Catered gourmet lunch on board the yacht — fresh seafood, charcuterie, salads, fruit, and premium Algarve wines
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina — premium tasting menu with full wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: This is the premium highlight of the trip. Book the private yacht charter well in advance — September is still peak season. Full-day charters typically run 8–10 hours. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light layer for the sea breeze. Snorkeling in the Algarve's clear waters is exceptional.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos — a leisurely walk to Ponta da Piedade, the most iconic clifftop viewpoint in Lagos, just 2km from the hotel. Watch the morning light illuminate the golden limestone formations and turquoise sea below. Take the steps down to the small beach for a final swim in the Atlantic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a relaxed lunch. Spend the afternoon at leisure — final souvenir shopping in Lagos old town, visiting local boutiques for Portuguese ceramics, cork products, and artisan goods. Pack and prepare for departure. Optional: final spa treatment or pool relaxation at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the finest restaurant of the trip — revisit your favorite or try Restaurante Bon Vivant for a grand finale. Order the best bottle of wine from the cellar and reflect on an extraordinary 13 days in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — savor every bite
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Lagos café — petiscos (Portuguese tapas), local cheese, and a glass of wine
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner — premium seafood, black pork, and a celebrated bottle of Alentejo or Douro red wine

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the morning or late afternoon for the most dramatic light. Confirm checkout time with the hotel. Arrange private transfer to Faro Airport for the following day. Pack purchased wines carefully with protective wrapping.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a last leisurely breakfast at Boutique Taghostel. Take a final stroll through Lagos, stopping for a last pastel de nata and espresso at a local café. Check out of the hotel and board your pre-arranged private luxury transfer to Faro Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart from Faro Airport. Carry with you the memories of 13 extraordinary days — dramatic cliffs, crystal-clear waters, world-class wines, and the warmth of Algarvian hospitality.
day_by_day.evening: In transit — homeward bound

meals.breakfast: Final full Portuguese breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — fresh pastries, local honey, cheeses, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Airport dining or in-flight
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight for the transfer from Lagos to Faro Airport. Confirm private transfer booking the night before. Ensure all purchased wines and fragile souvenirs are properly packed. Consider enrolling in airport lounge access for a premium departure experience.
